terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to read tonight's log, start a new one and look up the log of one night.

tasks.title: Read the whole log
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 1` in `night_log.py`, write a function called `log_text` that takes the path of a log file, as text, and gives back everything in the file as one text, line ends included. Open the file on a `with` line, with `encoding="utf-8"`. Print what it gives back for `"radio_log.txt"`.

Check makes log files of its own in a copy of your workspace, an empty one and one with letters such as Ì among them, calls `log_text` with each one's path, and looks at what it gives back and at whether the file was closed.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on opening a file.
Open the file at the path the function is given, on a with line.
Read all of it, inside the with block.
Give back what you read.
hints: Use the path the function is given, not the name of the file in your workspace: Check gives it other files.
`with open(...) as name:` opens the file and closes it when the lines moved in under it end. `read()` gives back the whole file as one text, and a second `read()` gives back empty text.
The shape is `with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as log:` with `return log.read()` moved in under it.

tasks.title: The log, entry by entry
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 2`, write a function called `log_entries` that takes the path of a log file, as text, and gives back a list of its entries, in order: each line without the spaces and line end at its ends, and blank lines left out. For `"radio_log.txt"` it gives back four entries. Open the file on a `with` line, with `encoding="utf-8"`. Print what it gives back for `"radio_log.txt"`.

Check makes log files of its own, one with no line end after its last line and one saved on Windows, calls `log_entries` with each one's path, and looks at what it gives back and at whether the file was closed.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on going through a file line by line.
Make an empty list, then open the file and go through it with for.
Strip each line, and add it to the list when something is left.
Give back the list after the with block.
hints: Each line a for loop gives you keeps its line end, except perhaps the last line of the file. Cutting off the last character cuts a letter off a last line that has no line end.
`strip()` takes off the line end and spaces, whatever is there. An empty text after stripping was a blank line.
The shape is `for line in log:` with `entry = line.strip()` and `if entry != "":` and `entries.append(entry)` moved in under it, inside the `with` block.

tasks.title: Start a new log
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 3`, write a function called `start_log` that takes the path of a file, as text, and a title, and makes that file hold only the title on one line, followed by a line end. Whatever the file held before is gone, and a file that is not there yet is made. It gives nothing back. Open the file on a `with` line, with `encoding="utf-8"`. Call it for `"tonight.txt"` and `"Callout log, 3 December"`.

Check calls `start_log` with paths of its own, some for a file that already holds an old log and one for a file that is not there yet, and reads each file back afterwards.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on writing to a file.
Open the file for writing, the kind that empties it first.
Write the title and a line end.
Open tonight.txt in the editor after running the file to see what it holds.
hints: The second value given to `open` says what the file is opened for. One of them keeps what is there and writes after it; the one this task needs empties the file first.
`"w"` empties the file, or makes it, before writing. `write` adds no line end of its own, so the line end is part of the text you write.
The shape is `with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as log:` with `log.write(title + "\n")` moved in under it.

tasks.title: Add an entry
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 4`, write a function called `add_entry` that takes the path of a log file, as text, and one entry, and adds the entry as a new line at the end of the file, followed by a line end. Everything the file held before stays as it was. It gives nothing back. Open the file on a `with` line, with `encoding="utf-8"`. Call it for `"tonight.txt"` and `"21:02 BRAVO TWO: leaving the base"`, then look at `tonight.txt`.

Check calls `add_entry` with log files of its own, an empty one too, and reads each file back afterwards. Every file it gives ends with a line end, or is empty.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on adding to the end of a file.
Open the file for adding, the kind that keeps what is there.
Write the entry and a line end.
Run the file twice and look at tonight.txt each time.
hints: Opening a file with `"w"` empties it first, so the old entries are lost.
`"a"` opens a file for adding to its end and keeps what it holds. The line end is still yours to write.
The shape is `with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as log:` with `log.write(entry + "\n")` moved in under it.

tasks.title: The log for one day
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 5`, write the line that imports `Path` from `pathlib`. Then write a function called `day_entries` that takes a folder, as a `Path`, and a day as text, such as `"2026-12-01"`. That day's log is the file named the day and `.txt`, in that folder. It gives back the entries of that file, as `log_entries` gives them, or an empty list when the folder has no file for that day. Ask whether the file is there before you open it. You may use your `log_entries`. Print what it gives back for `Path("logs")` and `"2026-12-02"`, and for `Path("logs")` and `"2026-12-25"`.

Check makes folders and logs of its own, calls `day_entries` for days with a log and a day without one, and looks at what it gives back and at which file it opened. It gives your file its own `log_entries` first, so a mistake in Task 2 does not count here.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on paths.
Write the import line under the Task 5 comment.
Join the folder and the file's name into one Path.
Ask whether that file is there: give back an empty list when it is not, and its entries when it is.
hints: A `Path` cannot be joined to text with `+`. The file's name is the day followed by `.txt`.
A `/` between a `Path` and a name gives the Path of that name in the folder, and the Path's `exists()` method says whether a file is there.
The shape is `path = folder / f"{day}.txt"`, then `if not path.exists():` with `return []` under it, and `return log_entries(path)`.
